title: What contracts promised and what City monitors recorded, provider by provider
question: Where a City monitor checked a provider against the objectives in its contract, what did the monitor record, and what was the provider paid that year and the next?
finding: Public Health's contract monitors have published results for 240 programme reviews at 33 nonprofits covering fiscal years 2020 to 2023. Of 236 reviews that give a figure, 38% met every contracted performance objective and 72 met under 80%; of 61 given an overall score, 6 were scored below standard (1 or 2 on a 4-point scale). Those 33 nonprofits received $252.2 million of the $636.2 million Public Health paid nonprofits in fiscal year 2023. For homelessness contracts, 108 contract memos carry a performance history; 17 of them say whether contract objectives were met (8 met, 7 not all met or not fully reported) and none gives the figures.
how: Public Health: each programme row in the contract-compliance tables and monitoring reports attached to Health Commission contract items (2021 to 2024) gives an overall score from 1 (unacceptable) to 4 (commendable), the share of contracted performance objectives met and the share of contracted units of service delivered. The tables are read here from the text of each paper: a row is anchored on the comment written by the monitor, and the provider is the agency heading printed above it. Rows are grouped by provider and fiscal year reviewed. Homelessness: the sentence in each contract memo's performance history that mentions objectives. City money is what that department paid the organization in the fiscal year reviewed and in the next two. City money is taken from the Controller's nonprofit-spending table, which keeps contracted services only and leaves out other payments to the same organizations.
limits: These scores are recorded by the department that pays the provider, not by an outside body, and are published only for contracts that happened to come before a commission in these years; most contracts have no published score. Scoring was suspended for fiscal years 2020 and 2021 because of the pandemic, so those years usually show percentages without a score. City money is everything the department paid the organization, not only the programme reviewed. 64 table rows could not be tied to a provider and are left out; University of California programmes appear without money because the university is not in the nonprofit payment data.
